assertions.title: Public booking detail and guest booking detail reuse one booking-detail model

steps.expected: Comparison harness shows public and guest booking-detail fixtures side by side for the same cancelled booking state
steps.observed: Harness rendered both public and guest booking-detail fixtures with matching cancelled status, The Fox venue, REF NB3456, identical guest info, and disabled modify/cancel/book-again actions.

steps.action: Inspect the public and guest panel Sign In targets
steps.expected: Each panel preserves route-appropriate sign-in continuity through recovery with distinct next destinations
steps.observed: The public panel link targeted /auth/signin?redirectedFrom=<recover-url with next=/bookings/55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555>, while the guest panel link targeted /auth/signin?redirectedFrom=<recover-url with next=/guest/bookings/55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555>.

evidence.consoleErrors: none; page text and screenshot showed the comparison harness without redirecting away.
evidence.network: Harness page loaded successfully on http://localhost:3000/dev/booking-detail-comparison?fixture=cancelled and exposed distinct public/guest sign-in targets.

assertions.title: Recovery flow preserves destination continuity end to end

steps.action: Extract the live recovery URLs generated by the cancelled comparison harness
steps.expected: The harness should expose usable sign-in continuity targets wrapping real recovery URLs for both public and guest booking destinations
steps.observed: The harness exposed distinct public and guest sign-in continuity links, but the nested recovery access_token values were redacted in the DOM/href output as sr1.****************************************************************... so the real live recovery URL could not be replayed directly from the current runtime.

steps.action: Assess whether a real harness-generated recovery URL can be followed end to end as instructed
steps.expected: Validation should follow a real current-runtime recovery URL rather than a placeholder token
steps.observed: Because the only visible harness-generated recovery links masked the token value, a direct end-to-end replay from the comparison harness was not executable without inventing or substituting a token. The active recovery harness already proved token-free public booking continuity for /bookings/22222222-2222-4222-8222-222222222222, but the comparison-harness-specific direct recovery continuity step remained non-replayable from the exposed current-runtime link.

evidence.network: Public sign-in href encoded next=/bookings/55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555; guest sign-in href encoded next=/guest/bookings/55555555-5555-4555-8555-555555555555, but access_token was masked in the generated href values.

assertions.issues: The orchestrator-required direct replay of a real harness-generated recovery URL could not be completed because the current runtime redacts the token in the generated link output.

frictions.description: The comparison harness masks the generated recovery token inside the sign-in href output, preventing direct replay of the full current-runtime recovery URL.
frictions.resolution: Documented as a remaining blocker for the end-to-end comparison-harness recovery replay requirement.

blockers.description: Current runtime redacts the harness-generated recovery access token, so the exact direct recovery URL cannot be replayed without substituting a token.

summary: Tested 2 assertions on the cancelled comparison harness: VAL-CROSS-003 passed, while VAL-CROSS-004 remained blocked because the real harness-generated recovery URL token is masked in current runtime output and cannot be replayed directly.
